CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steven W. Huang, DDS, Mayor  www.SanMarinoCA.gov
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Tony Chou, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

Calvin Lo, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Steve Talt, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  FRIDAY, JUNE 28, 2024 AT 8:30 AM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

 The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
  with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

  Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
  adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

  In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
  requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626)
  300-0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov until 3:00
  p.m. the day before the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will
  be distributed to City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00

   p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not provided to City Council
  at the meeting.
  Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us
  teleconference module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted
  after the in-person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Talt, Vice Mayor Shepherd
Romey, and Mayor Huang

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.SanMarinoCA.gov.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to
place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

   PUBLIC HEARINGS

 1.  PUBLIC HEARING TO CONSIDER APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION OF
  THE SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL ORDERING THAT A MEASURE TO
  EXTEND THE CITY'S EXISTING PUBLIC SAFETY SPECIAL TAX FOR
  FOUR (4) YEARS BE SUBMITTED TO THE VOTERS AT THE GENERAL
  MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 5, 2024,
  AND DIRECTING THE CITY ATTORNEY TO PREPARE AN IMPARTIAL
  ANALYSIS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council conduct a public hearing and
  direct that a Measure be included on the November 5, 2024, election ballot that will
  give residents of the City of San Marino the opportunity to decide whether to
  continue the Special Public Safety Tax for paramedic, police, and fire protection
  services. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R-24-22, a resolution of the San Marino City Council
  ordering that a measure to extend the City’s existing Public Safety Special Tax for
  four (4) years be submitted to the voters at the general municipal election to be held
  on Tuesday, November 5, 2024, and directing the City Attorney to prepare an
  impartial analysis.”

  NEW BUSINESS

 2.  APPROVAL AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS PERTAINING TO THE
  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 5, 2024

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council adopt: (1) Resolution No. R-
  24-11 calling and giving notice of the holding of a General Municipal Election to be
  held on Tuesday, November 5, 2024, for the election of certain officers as required by
  the provisions of the laws of the State of California relating to General Law Cities and
  requesting the Registrar of Voters of the County of Los Angeles to conduct said
  election; (2) Resolution No. R-24-12 requesting the Board of Supervisors of the
  County of Los Angeles to render services to the City relating to the conduct of a
  General Municipal Election to be held on Tuesday, November 5, 2024; and (3)
  Resolution No. R-24-13 adopting regulations for candidates for elective office
  pertaining to candidates’ statements submitted to the voters at an election to be held
  on November 5, 2024. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution Nos. R-24-11, calling and giving notice of the holding of
  a General Municipal Election to be held on Tuesday, November 5, 2024; R-24-12,
  requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Los Angeles to render services
  to the City relating to the conduct of a General Municipal Election to be held on
  Tuesday, November 5, 2024; and R-24-13, adopting regulations for candidates for
  elective office pertaining to candidates’ statements submitted to the voters at the
  election to be held on November 5, 2024.”

  3.  ACCEPTANCE OF A $150,000 DONATION FROM THE HUNTINGTON
  LIBRARY, ART MUSEUM, AND BOTANICAL GARDENS FOR RECEIPT IN
  THE CAPITAL PROJECTS FUND

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council accept the donation and apply
  the funds to capital projects, the appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to accept the donation of $150,000 from the Huntington Library, Art
  Museum, and Botanical Gardens; authorize the Finance Department to receipt the
  donation in the Capital Projects Fund; and amend the FY 2023-24 revenue budget to
  recognize revenue of $150,000 in the Capital Projects Fund (Account # 394-00-3601-
  0000).”

 4.  APPROVAL OF A MASTER EQUITY LEASE AGREEMENT WITH
  ENTERPRISE FLEET MANAGEMENT, INC. FOR THE LEASING OF NEW
  FLEET VEHICLES, APPROVAL OF AN ASSIGNMENT AGREEMENT WITH
  ENTERPRISE FLEET MANAGEMENT, INC. FOR THE SALE OF CITY-
  OWNED  VEHICLES  REPLACED  THROUGH  THIS  PROGRAM,
  AUTHORIZATION FOR THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE
  AGREEMENTS  AND  COMPLETE  ANY  NECESSARY  FORMS,
  AUTHORIZATION FOR THE CITY MANAGER TO ADD, REMOVE, OR
  TRADE-IN FLEET VEHICLES AS APPROPRIATE AND SURPLUS TO BE
  SOLD BY ENTERPRISE FLEET MANAGEMENT, INC. PURSUANT TO THE
  ASSIGNMENT AGREEMENT AND IN COMPLIANCE WITH MUNICIPAL
  CODE SECTION 2.06.06, AND APPROVE THE LEASING AND
  DISPOSITION OF NEW FLEET VEHICLES AT THE CITY MANAGER’S
  DISCRETION CONSISTENT WITH OPERATIONAL NEEDS AND BUDGET
  ALLOCATION
  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council (1) approve a Master
  Equity Lease Agreement with Enterprise Fleet Management Inc. for the leasing of
  new fleet vehicles, (2) approve an Assignment Agreement with Enterprise Fleet
  Management Inc. for the sale of City owned vehicles replaced through this program,
  (3) authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and complete any
  necessary forms, (4) authorize the City Manager to add, remove, or trade-in fleet
  vehicles as appropriate and surplus to be sold by Enterprise Fleet Management, Inc.
  pursuant to the Assignment Agreement and in compliance with Municipal Code
  Section 2.06.06, and (5) approve the leasing and disposition of new fleet vehicles at
  the City Manager’s discretion consistent with operational needs and budget allocation.
  If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:
  “I move to (1) approve a Master Equity Lease Agreement with Enterprise Fleet
  Management Inc. for the leasing of new fleet vehicles, (2) approve an Assignment
  Agreement with Enterprise Fleet Management Inc. for the sale of City owned vehicles
  replaced through this program, (3) authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and complete any necessary forms, (4) authorize the City Manager to
  add, remove, or trade-in fleet vehicles as appropriate and surplus to be sold by
  Enterprise Fleet Management, Inc. pursuant to the Assignment Agreement and in
  compliance with Municipal Code Section 2.06.06, and (5) approve the leasing and
  disposition of new fleet vehicles at the City Manager’s discretion consistent with
  operational needs and budget allocation.”

   CONSENT CALENDAR

 5.  AMENDMENT TO THE AGREEMENT BETWEEN LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  AND THE CITY OF SAN MARINO FOR PARAMEDIC SERVICES

  Recommendation: Staff  recommends  the Council  approve  the  amended
  agreement between the City of San Marino and Los Angeles County Fire Department.
  If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation an appropriate motion would
  be:

  ”I move to approve Amendment Number One to the Agreement by and Between the
  Consolidated Fire Protection District of Los Angeles County and the City of San Marino
  for Paramedic Services and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement on
  behalf of the City.”

 6.  FIRE MANAGEMENT SHARED SERVICES AGREEMENT REVIEW (JULY
  2021 TO JUNE 2024)

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  ”I move to receive and file the review of the Fire Management Shared Services
  Agreement for the period of July 2021 to June 2024.”

 7.  APPROVAL OF FAMILY ASSISTANCE CENTER ANNEX TO THE CITY OF
  SAN MARINO'S EMERGENCY OPERATIONS PLAN

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt the Family Assistance Center
  Annex into the City of San Marino Emergency Operations Plan. If Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  ”I move to adopt the Family Assistance Center Annex into the City of San Marino
  Emergency Operations Plan.”

 8.  AUTHORIZATION TO DISPOSE OF SURPLUS PROPERTY BY PUBLIC
  AUCTION PER MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 2.06.06

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the disposal of surplus
  vehicles and equipment via public auction pursuant to Municipal Code Section
  2.06.06. If the Council concurs, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the disposal of surplus equipment as listed in the staff report via
  public auction, pursuant to Municipal Code Section 2.06.06.”

 WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.
